title: Complete Microsoft Office Mastery Professional Certificate
description: A full 20-module program from complete beginner to advanced Microsoft Office professional: Windows & files, Word, Excel (essentials & advanced), PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, Teams, OneDrive, Microsoft Copilot, collaboration, business documentation, data analysis, productivity, workplace communication, 10 real-world projects, a capstone and a Certificate of Completion.
outcomes: Manage Windows and files, and use OneDrive cloud storage
Create professional documents in Word and analyse data in Excel
Master advanced Excel: lookups, pivot tables and dashboards
Build presentations in PowerPoint and manage email/calendar in Outlook
Collaborate with OneNote and Teams and use Microsoft Copilot (AI)
Produce business documents and reports, and build an Office portfolio
about: This is the complete TIH Microsoft Office Mastery Professional Certificate, rebuilt into twenty modules that take you from complete beginner to advanced Office professional.

Every content lesson has a video and printable notes with downloadable templates and practice files; ten real-world projects and a capstone build an Office portfolio for professional and administrative roles.

Software & tools: Microsoft Windows, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, Teams, OneDrive, Copilot, Forms, Planner, To Do, Edge and Adobe Acrobat Reader. You finish with a portfolio and — after the graduation assessment — a Certificate of Completion, ready for MOS certification.
requirements: No prior experience required — we start from the basics
A computer with Microsoft Office (or Microsoft 365)
Willingness to practise each feature hands-on

faqs.question: Do I need to buy Microsoft Office?
faqs.answer: Microsoft 365 Personal costs about $70/year and includes all apps plus 1TB OneDrive storage. A free 30-day trial covers the entire course. Many employers also provide Office licenses.

faqs.question: Is this different from the Computer Literacy course?
faqs.answer: The Computer Literacy course covers Office at a basic introductory level. This course goes into advanced features of each application comprehensively, it's the deep-dive version.

faqs.question: Will Office skills help me get a job?
faqs.answer: Almost every office job in Liberia requires Word, Excel, and PowerPoint proficiency. Listing Microsoft Office competency on your CV is table stakes for administrative, finance, and management roles.

faqs.question: Does this cover Google Workspace too?
faqs.answer: This course focuses on Microsoft Office specifically. If you need Google Workspace skills, our Data Analytics course covers Google Sheets in detail.

instructor.name: Samuel Doe
instructor.title: Microsoft Certified Trainer & Productivity Expert
instructor.bio: Samuel Doe is a Microsoft Certified Trainer (MCT) with 15 years teaching Office productivity to businesses, government agencies, and NGOs across Liberia. He has helped over 5,000 professionals master the Microsoft Office suite.

Module 3: Microsoft Word EssentialsComplete lesson

📝 Table of Contents

This lesson teaches Table of Contents so you can create structured, readable, accessible, and professionally controlled Word documents. You will learn the meaning, workflow, quality checks, and a complete workplace application.

Workplace productivity model
📝 Table of Contents
1. Structure
2. Format
3. Review
4. Publish
Professional document

Definition

An automatic table of contents is generated from correctly applied heading styles and can be updated when pagination changes.

🔑 Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

Table of Contents

An automatic table of contents is generated from correctly applied heading styles and can be updated when pagination changes.

style

a named set of formatting rules applied consistently to document elements

section break

a boundary allowing part of a document to use different page settings

mail merge

a process that combines a standard document with a data source to create personalized copies

Detailed explanation

An automatic table of contents is generated from correctly applied heading styles and can be updated when pagination changes. A professional user begins with the audience and required result, chooses the correct tool and structure, protects source information, checks accuracy and accessibility, and delivers the work in the appropriate editable and final formats.

  • Styles create consistent structure and power navigation and tables of contents.
  • Page layout controls margins, orientation, sections, headers, and footers.
  • Tables communicate structured data; images require captions and alternative text.
  • Track Changes and comments support review without losing accountability.

Step-by-step application

  1. Structure: clarify the purpose, audience, source information, required output, and deadline.
  2. Format: create the work with consistent structure, accurate content, and controlled file names.
  3. Review: review formulas, facts, layout, accessibility, permissions, and feedback.
  4. Publish: deliver or share the approved version, confirm receipt or action, and archive the source.

Worked workplace example

A small organization prepares a five-page proposal with heading styles, numbered pages, a table, image captions, references, a generated contents page, and PDF export.

Completed example: Apply Heading 1 to major sections, Heading 2 to subsections, insert an automatic table of contents, and update it before exporting the PDF.

Professional quality checklist

  • Purpose and requested action are immediately clear.
  • Names, dates, amounts, calculations, sources, spelling, and attachments are checked.
  • Heading structure, contrast, reading order, and alternative text support accessibility.
  • File name, format, version, storage location, and sharing permission are correct.
  • Sensitive information is minimized and protected.

Guided practice with detailed answer

Question: How should an office professional use Table of Contents to improve a training program’s monthly report?

Answer: First confirm the report’s audience, decision, deadline, and approved source data. Apply Table of Contents using a consistent structure and clear ownership. Verify every number, name, date, formula, chart label, link, and claim against the source. Ask another person to review the output when the risk of error is high. Correct accessibility and permission issues, export the required final format, share it only with authorized recipients, request the specific next action, and retain the editable source and approved version according to the organization’s filing rules.

Summary

Table of Contents belongs to Microsoft Word Essentials. A competent learner can define it, apply it to realistic work, verify accuracy and accessibility, protect information, and deliver a professional result.

Office habit: Before sending, check the reader, result, numbers, names, dates, attachments, permissions, and required next action.

Definition

🔑 Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

Task Management

Task Management is a productivity & time management concept or skill used to create, organize, analyze, communicate, collaborate, or deliver workplace information effectively.

time blocking

reserving calendar periods for specific categories of work

workflow

a repeatable sequence through which information or work moves

automation

technology that performs a defined recurring action with limited manual effort

Detailed explanation

Task Management is a productivity & time management concept or skill used to create, organize, analyze, communicate, collaborate, or deliver workplace information effectively. A professional user begins with the audience and required result, chooses the correct tool and structure, protects source information, checks accuracy and accessibility, and delivers the work in the appropriate editable and final formats.

  • A productivity system should reduce forgotten commitments and decision friction.
  • Priorities reflect importance and impact, not only urgency.
  • Calendar blocks protect time; task lists define actions.
  • Automation should be simple, documented, reversible, and periodically checked.

Step-by-step application

  1. Capture: clarify the purpose, audience, source information, required output, and deadline.
  2. Prioritize: create the work with consistent structure, accurate content, and controlled file names.
  3. Schedule: review formulas, facts, layout, accessibility, permissions, and feedback.
  4. Review: deliver or share the approved version, confirm receipt or action, and archive the source.

Worked workplace example

A staff member collects commitments in one task system, assigns deadlines and priorities, time-blocks focused work, batches email, uses safe automation, and reviews progress weekly.

Completed example: Turn “Prepare report” into actions: confirm data, clean table, calculate KPIs, draft findings, review with manager, and submit by Friday.

Professional quality checklist

  • Purpose and requested action are immediately clear.
  • Names, dates, amounts, calculations, sources, spelling, and attachments are checked.
  • Heading structure, contrast, reading order, and alternative text support accessibility.
  • File name, format, version, storage location, and sharing permission are correct.
  • Sensitive information is minimized and protected.

Guided practice with detailed answer

Question: How should an office professional use Task Management to improve a training program’s monthly report?

Answer: First confirm the report’s audience, decision, deadline, and approved source data. Apply Task Management using a consistent structure and clear ownership. Verify every number, name, date, formula, chart label, link, and claim against the source. Ask another person to review the output when the risk of error is high. Correct accessibility and permission issues, export the required final format, share it only with authorized recipients, request the specific next action, and retain the editable source and approved version according to the organization’s filing rules.

Summary

Task Management belongs to Productivity & Time Management. A competent learner can define it, apply it to realistic work, verify accuracy and accessibility, protect information, and deliver a professional result.

lessons.title: 20.1 Certificate Requirements
lessons.html:
Module 1: Course OrientationComplete lesson

🧭 Certificate Requirements

This lesson teaches Certificate Requirements so you can understand the Microsoft 365 workplace ecosystem, course path, learning evidence, and responsible digital practice. You will learn the meaning, workflow, quality checks, and a complete workplace application.

Workplace productivity model
🧭 Certificate Requirements
1. Learn
2. Create
3. Review
4. Share

Definition

Certificate Requirements is a course orientation concept or skill used to create, organize, analyze, communicate, collaborate, or deliver workplace information effectively.

🔑 Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

Certificate Requirements

Certificate Requirements is a course orientation concept or skill used to create, organize, analyze, communicate, collaborate, or deliver workplace information effectively.

Microsoft 365

a subscription ecosystem of productivity applications, cloud services, security, and collaboration features

productivity suite

a collection of applications used to create, analyze, communicate, organize, and collaborate

digital workflow

a connected sequence of digital tasks, information, approvals, and outputs

Detailed explanation

Certificate Requirements is a course orientation concept or skill used to create, organize, analyze, communicate, collaborate, or deliver workplace information effectively. A professional user begins with the audience and required result, chooses the correct tool and structure, protects source information, checks accuracy and accessibility, and delivers the work in the appropriate editable and final formats.

  • Microsoft 365 combines desktop, web, mobile, cloud, communication, and collaboration tools.
  • Choose an application according to the work product and audience.
  • Professional work must be accurate, accessible, secure, and easy to update.
  • Practice files should demonstrate real decisions rather than empty features.

Step-by-step application

  1. Learn: clarify the purpose, audience, source information, required output, and deadline.
  2. Create: create the work with consistent structure, accurate content, and controlled file names.
  3. Review: review formulas, facts, layout, accessibility, permissions, and feedback.
  4. Share: deliver or share the approved version, confirm receipt or action, and archive the source.

Worked workplace example

A learner prepares a professional portfolio containing a letter, budget workbook, presentation, meeting invitation, shared folder, and final workplace project.

Completed example: Create a folder named TIH-Office-Portfolio with subfolders for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Communication, and Final Project.

Professional quality checklist

  • Purpose and requested action are immediately clear.
  • Names, dates, amounts, calculations, sources, spelling, and attachments are checked.
  • Heading structure, contrast, reading order, and alternative text support accessibility.
  • File name, format, version, storage location, and sharing permission are correct.
  • Sensitive information is minimized and protected.

Guided practice with detailed answer

Question: How should an office professional use Certificate Requirements to improve a training program’s monthly report?

Answer: First confirm the report’s audience, decision, deadline, and approved source data. Apply Certificate Requirements using a consistent structure and clear ownership. Verify every number, name, date, formula, chart label, link, and claim against the source. Ask another person to review the output when the risk of error is high. Correct accessibility and permission issues, export the required final format, share it only with authorized recipients, request the specific next action, and retain the editable source and approved version according to the organization’s filing rules.

Summary

Certificate Requirements belongs to Course Orientation. A competent learner can define it, apply it to realistic work, verify accuracy and accessibility, protect information, and deliver a professional result.

Office habit: Before sending, check the reader, result, numbers, names, dates, attachments, permissions, and required next action.

questions.explanation: Backups guard against data loss.

questions.question: Good folder organization means:
questions.explanation: Structured folders make files easy to find.

questions.question: OneDrive integration lets Windows:
options: Sync your files to the cloud automatically
questions.explanation: OneDrive syncs files to the cloud and other devices.

questions.question: A file extension like .docx tells you:
questions.explanation: Extensions indicate the file type and app.

questions.question: To make text bold in Word you press:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+B toggles bold.

questions.question: A Table of Contents in Word is built from:
questions.explanation: Word generates a TOC from Heading 1/2/3 styles.

questions.question: Mail Merge is used to:
options: Create many personalised documents from a data list
questions.explanation: Mail Merge personalises letters/labels for many recipients.
